verdicts.reason: Both break the product: the cream circle has come loose to the bottom-left corner, cut off by the canvas edge, and the jar is just a hollow outline floating above it. A keeps the headline on one line, but it nearly runs into the Try It button, which is jammed against the right edge. B wraps the headline onto two clean lines and leaves more room around the button, so its spacing is slightly better.

Both have the same broken product (loose cream circle in the corner, hollow jar outline). A also shrinks Try It to a tiny pill dropped to the lower right, lined up with nothing, so the call to action is buried. B keeps a large button level with the headline, so the hierarchy is right.

A has the shared flaw of a broken product image (loose circle, hollow jar), but the copy and button hold up. B effectively loses the product: the jar is shrunk to a speck in the bottom right, and the cream circle crowds right under 'Out now.' The left-heavy text over a large empty middle has no focal image, so the brand fidelity is gone.
